vignette: 70-year-old man resuscitated from out-of-hospital cardiac arrest due to ventricular fibrillation. Serial troponins and coronary angiography showed no acute MI and no culprit lesion; electrolytes, drug levels and toxicology were normal and no other transient or reversible cause was found. Echocardiogram LVEF 45%. Requesting an initial ICD. He is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia.
rationale_note: Secondary prevention after VF arrest; shared decision making is not required for B1.

vignette: 68-year-old woman with ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy after an anterior MI 2 years ago, NYHA class II heart failure, LVEF 30% on echocardiography. No CABG or PCI in the past year; recent angiography found no lesions suitable for revascularization. No history of sustained VT or cardiac arrest. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD. She is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia. Before implantation, a nurse practitioner held a shared decision-making encounter using an evidence-based ICD decision tool.
rationale_note: Ischemic cardiomyopathy, NYHA II, LVEF 30% by echo, MI 2 years ago.

vignette: 64-year-old man with a large anterior MI 21 days ago, now with LVEF 25% on echocardiography and NYHA class II symptoms; no revascularization targets remain and no pacemaker indication. No sustained VT or cardiac arrest. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD now. He is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia. Before implantation, a nurse practitioner held a shared decision-making encounter using an evidence-based ICD decision tool.
rationale_note: MI 21 days ago: inside the 40-day waiting period; no pacemaker indication.

vignette: 55-year-old woman with newly diagnosed non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, LVEF 30% on cardiac MRI, NYHA class III. Normal coronary angiogram. Guideline-directed medical therapy was started 6 weeks ago. No sustained VT or cardiac arrest. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD. She is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia. Before implantation, a nurse practitioner held a shared decision-making encounter using an evidence-based ICD decision tool.
rationale_note: Non-ischemic cardiomyopathy on GDMT for only 6 weeks (needs >= 3 months).

vignette: 61-year-old man with non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, LVEF 28% on echocardiography, NYHA class II despite 5 months of optimal medical therapy. Normal coronary angiogram; no sustained VT or cardiac arrest. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD. The record contains no documentation of a shared decision-making encounter about the ICD. He is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia.
rationale_note: Primary prevention without a documented shared decision-making encounter.

vignette: 72-year-old man with ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy, LVEF 25% on echocardiography, NYHA class II, MI 3 years ago, no revascularization options. He was recently diagnosed with metastatic pancreatic cancer; his oncologist estimates survival of 4-6 months. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD. He is clinically stable with no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation. Before implantation, a nurse practitioner held a shared decision-making encounter using an evidence-based ICD decision tool.
rationale_note: Metastatic pancreatic cancer with expected survival of months.

vignette: 66-year-old woman who had a ventricular fibrillation arrest with a potassium of 2.1 mmol/L after high-dose diuretic use; potassium was corrected and she has had no further arrhythmia. No acute MI; structurally normal heart with LVEF 60% on echocardiography. Requesting a secondary-prevention ICD. She is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia.
rationale_note: VF arrest caused by severe hypokalemia: transient/reversible cause.

vignette: 74-year-old man with an ICD implanted 9 years ago for sustained ventricular tachycardia; the device has reached its elective replacement indicator. LVEF on his latest echocardiogram is 50%. Requesting ICD generator replacement. He is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia.
rationale_note: Replacement at ERI; current LVEF 50% and absence of a new SDM encounter do not matter.

vignette: 45-year-old woman with genetically confirmed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, maximal wall thickness 31 mm, unexplained syncope, and a family history of sudden cardiac death; her cardiologist documents high risk of life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia. LVEF 65% on cardiac MRI. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD. She is clinically stable, not in shock, with no significant brain damage, no non-cardiac disease limiting survival to under a year, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation or other supraventricular tachycardia. Before implantation, a nurse practitioner held a shared decision-making encounter using an evidence-based ICD decision tool.
rationale_note: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: genetic high-risk disorder with SDM.

vignette: 79-year-old man with an MI 4 years ago, LVEF 25% on echocardiography, and NYHA class IV heart failure with symptoms at rest despite therapy; he is not a transplant or LVAD candidate and angiography shows no revascularization targets. No sustained VT or cardiac arrest. Requesting a primary-prevention ICD. He is not in shock, has no non-cardiac life-limiting disease, and no poorly rate-controlled atrial fibrillation. Before implantation, a nurse practitioner held a shared decision-making encounter using an evidence-based ICD decision tool.
rationale_note: Prior MI with LVEF 25% but NYHA class IV (excluded from B2; B3 also requires NYHA II-III).
